Hermetic magic cannot restore physical energy (Exhaustion Levels), nor can it restore self-confidence (Confidence). Most magi believe this to be a flaw in Hermetic theory.

#### Limit of the Infernal {#limit-of-the-infernal}

Intellego magic is almost completely useless against the Infernal, as it only reveals what the demons want you to believe, whether it is true or not. The source of this limit is hotly debated. Optimists believe it is a limitation of Hermetic theory. Pessimists believe it stems from the Limit of the Divine. Moderates believe it stems from the Limit of Essential Nature, as deception is the nature of demons, so if you use Intellego against them, you will only discover their deceptions. Heretical magi point out that, thanks to this limit, there is no way to distinguish between God and a very powerful demon.

#### Limit of the Lunar Sphere {#limit-of-the-lunar-sphere}

Hermetic magic cannot affect the Lunar Sphere or anything above it. Most magi believe that this stems from the Limit of the Divine. The Lunar Sphere is the innermost of the celestial spheres carrying the stars and planets in their orbits around the Earth, and this restriction rarely affects magi.

#### Limit of the Soul {#limit-of-the-soul}

Hermetic magic cannot affect an immortal soul, and therefore cannot create true human life or restore the dead to life. Most magi believe this stems from the Limit of the Divine, although a significant number believe that Hermetic magic's inability to raise the dead merely reflect a flaw in the theory. Animals do not have immortal souls and can therefore be created. Magical creatures and faeries are generally believed not to have immortal souls, and there are spells that appear to create them, but some magi believe that such spells actually summon existing creatures. Angels and demons are nothing more than immortal souls, but can be affected by Vim.

#### Limit of Time {#limit-of-time}

Hermetic magic is incapable of changing the course of time. It cannot affect anything in the past, and can only affect the future by making changes in the present. This limit also means that Hermetic magic cannot predict the past or the future (other magic is required for this). Most magicians believe that this stems from the Limit of the Divine.

#### Limit of True Feeling {#limit-of-true-feeling}

A few humans have a love, friendship, or faith that Hermetic magic cannot influence in any way. Magi agree that this must stem from one of the two fundamental Limits, since most emotions can be influenced by magic, but they disagree on which one.

#### Limit of Vis {#limit-of-vis}

Hermetic magic cannot change the Art with which raw wisdom is affiliated. Most magicians believe that this is a result of the Restriction of Essential Nature.

#### Limit of Warping {#limit-of-warping}

Prolonged exposure to active magic or high auras usually causes changes, generally referred to as warping (or distortion). Hermetic magic is completely incapable of affecting these changes once they have occurred. Magical Twilight is a manifestation of warping. Most magicians would like to believe that this stems from the Limit of the Divine, as it would make magic a manifestation of Divine power. Others believe that it stems from the Limit of Essential Nature.

## Original Research {#original-research}

Many magi (but primarily House Bonisagus) feel that original research is the core of Hermetic magic, and the true passion of Bonisagus, continuing the Founder's ingenuity by pushing the boundaries of magic. Several also believe that this is the best way to fulfill the specifications of the Hermetic Oath, and that it is their duty to explore the unspoken mysteries of magic. Others strive to push the boundaries of magic for vain reasons, hoping to attach their name to a discovery that will live on long after their Longevity ritual has failed them.

A magician can begin original research at any point in their career. Some wait and increase their knowledge of the Hermetic Arts to strengthen their abilities in the laboratory, while others begin as soon as they leave their apprenticeship. There are no minimum requirements for Art or Ability to undertake original research, and the process is the same whether the magician is a wise old archimagus or a curious youth.

Original research often takes several years and can be done in three tiers depending on how significant an undertaking you want to do:

### Minor Breakthroughs {#minor-breakthroughs}

A Minor Breakthrough is something that can be immediately used and taught within the existing framework of Hermetic magic. For example, a new Range or a new Duration for spells than those that already exist. Minor Breakthroughs could be more common, but they are rare because most magi (especially Bonisagi) have grander goals. Why invent a new Range when you can try to break a Hermetic Limit? Grandiosity often drives magi toward more difficult projects.

### Major Breakthroughs {#major-breakthroughs}

A Major Breakthrough pushes the boundaries of Magic Theory without actually breaking them. New Magic Virtues, incorporation of some kind of primitive magic into the Hermetic tradition, etc. A Major Breakthrough can also allow you to adapt a standard application of a Hermetic idea in a new way. Notatus' development of the Aegis of the Hearth was a Major Breakthrough, an advanced variant based on Bonisagus' Parma Magica. A Major Breakthrough will make the magician famous.

### Hermetic Breakthroughs {#hermetic-breakthroughs}

A Hermetic Breakthrough is a new arcane ability or something that breaks one of the fundamental Limits of Magic, such as magic affecting the lunar sphere, true resurrection of the dead, etc. These are extremely rare and difficult. Almost anything could be possible; this is magic in its most unexplored state. Examples of possible new arcane abilities could be, in practice, sending mental images from one magician's mind to another (i.e., raw telepathy) or an ability to pass through different levels of regiones without the use of spells.

Breaking one of the Lesser Limits on Hermetic magic is a very difficult but achievable goal, which could definitely change the nature of magic in the saga. Officially, Parma Magica is the only Hermetic Breakthrough that has occurred in the 450 years of the  Order, but there are suspicions that others may have occurred.

# Nomenclature {#nomenclature}

| Game Term | Explanation |
| ----- | ----- |
| Arcane Connection (AC) | A magical link (usually an object associated with or derived from part of the target) that makes it possible to influence something or someone at a distance. A Hermetic magician can use it to cast spells at the target across any distance, and to push those spells through Magic Resistance. |
| Artes Liberales, Liberal Arts | The seven liberal arts, the basis of medieval academic education. Important for Hermetic magic and academic studies. Artes Liberales are divided into two groups: Trivium (grammar, logic, and rhetoric) and Quadrivium (arithmetic, geometry, astronomy, and music). |
| Aura | An area with a specific magical, divine, infernal, or faerie-based presence. |
| Spell Mastery | In-depth knowledge and skill in a specific formulaic spell. |
| Botch | Magic is always unpredictable. The most common danger is that the magician makes a serious mistake that not only fails the spell, but has other unforeseen effects \- usually negative. Magicians who botch spells incur Warping and, in more serious cases, may end up in Magical Twilight. |
| Hedge Wizard | A condescending term used within the Order for outsider magicians. |
| Ceremonial Casting | A technique for spontaneous magic where spending time casting the spell  in a structured and ceremonial way can increase its power or chances of success. 15 minutes per magnitude. |
| Certamen | Magical duel between magi to resolve disputes. Normally does not cause damage (taboo), but the winner may choose to cast a spell on the opponent. |
| Covenant | The place where a group of magi and their followers live and work together. |
| Diedne | The rejected House, known for its druidic roots and later accused of diabolism and human sacrifice. Wiped out in the Schism War that nearly tore the Order apart in the early 11th century. |
| Dominion | The divine magical aura, and the area under divine influence. Dominion spreads everywhere where the clergy operates, both in cities and in cultivated countryside. It becomes stronger near or in sanctuaries. Church bells effectively spread Dominion. |
| Domus Magna | The headquarters of a magical House. Normally the leading covenant. |
| Durenmar | The first covenant founded by Bonisagus, located in the Black Forest (Schwarzwald) in the Rhine Tribunal. |
| Enigma | A central philosophy within House Criamon involving the understanding of the secrets of the universe. |
| Familiar | A magical animal that is closely bound to a magician and shares some of their powers and life. |
| Faerie | Creatures and powers of the Faerie Realm. These are often capricious, sometimes malicious. They always care about humans, but sometimes in the way a torturer cares about his victim. They hold fast to agreements and covenants. House Merinita in particular focuses on faeries and faerie magic. |
| Filius/Filia/Filii | Man/Woman/Plural. A disciple who has become a fully-fledged magician. One becomes the filius of one's teacher, and sometimes this is used as a suffix to one's name. |
| Scrying | Using magic to monitor or spy on someone from a distance. Prohibited and highly taboo to do against magicians within the Order. |
| Forms | The essential natural phenomena that Hermetic magic can manipulate. The forms are: Animal, Aquam, Auram, Corpus, Herbam, Ignem, Imaginem, Mentem, Terram, and Vim. |
| Formulaic magic,Formulaic spell | This type of magic is based on carefully crafted and learned spells, which are specifically designed and prepared to achieve predictable and reliable results. The magic is powerful and effective, but not particularly flexible. It requires study and practice, and magi are limited to the spells they have learned and memorized in advance. |
| Gauntlet | The Gauntlet is a central ritual and trial that an apprentice must undergo to become a full-fledged Hermetic magus. It marks the end of formal training and the beginning of independent magician life. Each House within the Hermetic Order has its own unique traditions and requirements for the Gauntlet. |
| Grog | Ordinary people who serve and protect a covenant. |
| The Founders | The original 13 magicians who founded the Order of Hermes. |
| The Gift | The unusual ability to use almost all forms of magic, provided with the right training. All magicians have the Gift. The Gift makes people around them uncomfortable and more suspicious. It causes a negative modifier of \-3 to all social interactions with mundanes, and makes animals extremely uneasy. |
| Aegis of the Hearth | A special ritual, known only to the Order, that protects a covenant from magical intrusion. It needs to be cast once a year at significant cost of vis. |
| Code of Hermes | The laws that govern Hermetic magi and their accepted behaviors within the Order. |
| Order of Hermes, Hermetic Order, The Order | Almost all powerful magicians in Europe in the 13th century are members of the Hermetic Order of Hermes. |
| Hermetic Magic | The magical tradition founded by Bonisagus, inspired by Hermes Trismegistus and used by all magi of the Order. |
| Hermetic Arts | The magical disciplines on which magic is based, divided into 5 Techniques and 10 Forms. |
| Hoplite | The "muscle" and enforcers of the Order when violence is needed. They often hunt down diabolists (who are most often killed immediately) and criminals who do not comply with the quaesitors. Quaesitors sometimes have hoplites in tow if they need to conduct riskier investigations or if the magician they are investigating is expected to cause trouble. Many hoplites are from House Flambeau. |
| Court Wizards | Magicians who work for nobles and kings, often in violation of Hermetic laws, or outside of the Order. |
| House | The twelve groups within the Hermetic Order, each with its own philosophy and tradition. |
| Laboratory Text | A written account of how a specific magical effect (usually a spell) is achieved. Normally, a magician automatically creates a lab text when conducting magical research. However, in order for it to be useful to other magicians, it needs to be transcribed (seasonal work). |
| Laboratory | A magical laboratory where magicians conduct research, experiment, create spells, enchant objects, extract wisdom, etc. A magician normally spends most of their time there, and without a laboratory, the magician becomes quite handicapped. |
| Charged Item | Magical items that can be used once or a limited number of times before their power is depleted. The advantage is that they do not cost wisdom to create, but they are still seasonal work. |
| Apprentice | An apprentice trained by a magician. Normally, only one apprentice is taken at a time, and it takes about 15 years. It is a significant investment, but they are still sought after as they can be used for all kinds of tasks and magical assistance at least until they graduate. |
| Longevity Ritual | A ritual that extends a magician's life and counteracts aging. The ritual is always specific and unique to the magician. |
| Magus/Maga/Magi | Male/Female/Plural. Latin for magician. Often used within the Order. |
| Gentle Gift | A trait that prevents the magician's Gift from causing mistrust among mundane people. Simplifies social interactions. |
| Mundane | Ordinary people without magical powers. |
| Mystery Cults | The secret societies within the Order that have specialized magical knowledge. Four of the Houses are Mystery Cults: Bjornaer, Criamon, Merinita, Verditius |
| Parens | Magicians who have trained an apprentice. The title is only used after the apprenticeship period. The master becomes the parens of the newly qualified magician. |
| Parma Magica | A special magical protection spell that protects magicians from hostile magic and the effects of other magicians' Gifts. It is personal and expires at dawn and dusk, at which point the magician normally recasts it immediately. It takes about one diameter (2 minutes). Parma Magica is the Order's special secret and gives them an advantage over all other magicians.  |
| Penetration | The ability to overcome an opponent's magical protection when casting a spell. |
| Praeco | Honorary title for the chairperson of a Tribunal meeting. Normally given to the oldest magician present. |
| Primus/Prima/Primi | Man/Woman/Plural. The leader of a House. |
| Quaesitor | A magician trained in interpreting and upholding Hermetic laws, who has been granted the authority to act as an investigator. Most quaesitors are from House Guernicus, but promising magicians from other Houses can also become Quaesitors. A Quaesitor investigates violations of the Code and presents legal cases before the Tribunal. |
| Regiones | Singular: Regio. Places, areas, or entire worlds with an Aura of one of the four Realms that are completely or partially separated from our ordinary world. |
| Realm | The four supernatural powers: the Divine, the Magical, the Faeries, or the Infernal. |
| Ritual Magic | Powerful and complex magical ceremonies that often require significant resources and time to perform. Rituals always come at a cost. |
| Redcap | Messengers of House Mercere. House members usually wear red hats as a tradition. |
| Voting Sigil | A symbol representing a magician's vote in Tribunal matters. Within House Tremere, a master holds the voting sigils of his disciples in descending order until he is defeated in the Certamen or dies. The sigils are highly concentrated there. In some tribunals, magisters and archmages have more votes than newly hatched magicians. |
| Sanctum | A magician's private and protected sanctuary. Normally contains both living quarters and a laboratory. |
| True Faith | Deep and genuine belief in a higher power, usually God, which provides a certain degree of protection against magic and other supernatural forces. This protection comes from strong, unwavering spirituality and faith, which is not just a formal religious belief, but is so deep and true that it has concrete effects on the individual's destiny and abilities. |
| True Lineages | Those Houses within the Order of Hermes that have an unbroken chain of teachers and disciples going back to the founders. (Bonisagus, Guernicus, Mercere, Tremere) |
| Wizards Sigil | All magic used by a magician leaves a personal imprint on the place or its target (think of it as a fingerprint). It can be used to see that magic has been used and also to track down who performed it (Quaesitors are specialists in this). There are techniques for trying to distort or hide one's magical sigil, but they are not entirely perfect. |
| The Schism War | The terrible civil war in the early 11th century that wiped out House Diedne and nearly tore the Order apart. |
| Twilight | A state in which a magician loses contact with the physical world and becomes one with magic, which can happen when the magician loses control of their magic. The state can last from seconds to several years. Over time, older magicians become more and more "vulnerable" to Twilight \- often to the point of disappearing into the Final Twilight. Only Criamon actively seeks the state of Twilight. |
| Final Twilight | The permanent state in which a magician loses contact with the physical world and becomes one with magic, without returning. |
| Fast Casting | Quickly and reactively casting a spell in response to an immediate event or threat. |
| Sodalis | Singular, plural: *sodales*. A formal term for members of the same covenant or Order. I.e., sibling, friend, comrade. The word is used among equals, emphasizing that all Hermetic magicians are equal within the Order (although it is always the case that some are more equal than others). |
| Spontaneous Magic | Spontaneous magic offers magi a flexible and immediate method of using magic without preparation. Although less powerful and stable than Formulaic Magic, its ability to adapt to a variety of situations and problems is invaluable to Hermetic magi. |
| Sympathetic Connection | When one has some knowledge or contact with the target of a spell, one can use sympathetic links to increase one's chance of penetrating magical resistance. Examples: The target's signature, birth name, secret names, daily horoscope, birth horoscope, or a representation such as an image or figure. However, baptismal names cannot be used because the Divine Power prevents this. |
| Talisman | A very personal magical object that helps a magician concentrate and focus magical power. It can also be enchanted with specific effects. A magician can only have one Talisman, and it is always considered part of the magician, and is therefore also a two-way arcane connection. |
| Techniques | The five basic magical manipulations: Creo, Intellego, Muto, Perdo, and Rego. |
| Token | A physical token that allows a magician or creature of Might to be accepted by the Aegis of the Hearth (and thus not restricted by it), even if they were not present at the ritual itself. Normally, the number of tokens is limited and careful track is kept for obvious reasons. |
| Tribunal | A meeting where magi from a certain region (also called a Tribunal) gather to make decisions and judge disputes. Normally, a regional Tribunal is held every seven years. Every 33 years, the 13 regions of the Order  send their representatives to the Grand Tribunal, which is held at Durenmar in the Black Forest  (Schwarzwald). |
| Wizard's March | A formal declaration that a magician is excommunicated and can be hunted and killed by other members of the Order. Some magi of the Order specialize in this, since traditionally, whoever kills a marched magician can lay claim to all of their belongings. |
| Warping | Changes that occur during prolonged exposure to magical forces or high auras (6+). Powerful magic (level 30+) can cause immediate warping. |
| Vis | Magical energy in physical form used to perform powerful magic and permanent effects. Ritual magic requires vis. Vis is the most valuable thing for most magi and it's the hard currency of the Order. |
| Blatant Gift | The magician's magical Gift causes stronger distrust among ordinary people and direct hostility among animals. Penalty \-6 on social interactions. |
